record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: If f(x) is a one-variable complex polynomial with exactly k monomials, determine whether there exists an integer N(k) such that the vanishing of the moments ∫₀¹ f(x)^n dx for all 1 ≤ n ≤ N(k) already forces f to be zero.

evidence.quote: Problem 27. (i) Let f(x) be a polynomial in C[x] with k monomials. Is there a value N(k) such that if the following ﬁnite set of moment conditions hold: Mn := ∫1 0 fn(x) dx = 0, 1≤n≤N(k), then f = 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k\ge 1$ be a positive integer. For a polynomial $f\in\mathbb{C}[x]$, write $f$ as a sum of monomials and call $f$ a $k$-fewnomial if it has at most $k$ nonzero terms. For each integer $n\ge 1$ define the moment $M_n(f):=\int_0^1 f(x)^n\,dx$.

Question: Does there exist a positive integer $N(k)$, depending only on $k$, with the following property? For every $k$-fewnomial $f\in\mathbb{C}[x]$, if $M_n(f)=0$ for all integers $n$ with $1\le n\le N(k)$, then $f\equiv 0$.

Determine whether such an $N(k)$ exists, and if so, give an explicit bound for $N(k)$ in terms of $k$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is part of the circle of moment / composition-condition questions connected to the Poincaré center-focus problem for Abel equations. While related composition conjectures have been resolved (with counterexamples and partial positive results), no explicit bound $N(k)$ controlling finite-moment vanishing for arbitrary $k$-fewnomials appears to be known; the problem appears to remain open in this finite-detection form.

status_evidence.title: A counterexample to the composition condition conjecture for polynomial Abel differential equations
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexample to a related composition condition conjecture, showing the moment/composition landscape is subtle.
status_evidence.claim: Related composition-type conjectures have had counterexamples, but the finite-moment-detection question for k-fewnomials is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Center conditions, compositions of polynomials and moments on algebraic curves
status_evidence.snippet: Studies moments of polynomials in connection with center conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related moment problems are active research; finite detection by N(k) for k-fewnomials is not established.
